title: Folding and ring modulation
learned: A wavefolder adds overtones by folding the wave back when it gets too big
An envelope on FOLD CV makes the colour grow and fade with each note
A ring modulator multiplies two signals: slow B = tremolo, audio-rate B = bells
An LFO fast enough to hear is an oscillator: audio and CV are the same voltages

steps.why: Subtractive synthesis starts bright and takes away. The opposite approach starts with a pure sine, which has no overtones at all, and adds them. This is how many 'West Coast' synths work.
steps.do: Notes play from SIN of the oscillator: a pure, soft tone. In the rack there is a wavefolder (JX-FLD) and a ring modulator (JX-RNG). Press Next.

steps.why: A wavefolder turns the wave back down whenever it would go too high, again and again. Every fold adds a corner, and corners are overtones.
steps.do: Hold Ctrl and drag a new cable from SIN of the oscillator to IN of the wavefolder, then drag OUT of the wavefolder to IN 1 of the amplifier (it replaces the cable from SIN there).
steps.after: The sine got brighter and buzzier: FOLD starts at 30 %, already a few folds.

steps.why: FOLD sets how many times the wave is folded.
steps.do: Press F1 and turn FOLD of the wavefolder up and down.
steps.after: More folds, more overtones: from soft to brassy to metallic. Unlike a filter sweep, the tone changes character, not just brightness.
steps.try: Turn SYMMETRY: uneven folds sound hollower.

steps.why: Like the filter, the folder gets more alive when an envelope moves it.
steps.do: Press F2, hold Ctrl and drag a second cable from ENV of the envelope to FOLD CV of the wavefolder. Then press F1 and turn the FOLD CV knob up.
steps.after: Each note starts rich and settles to a softer tone: the envelope adds folds at the start of the note. Turn FOLD down a little to hear the movement better.

steps.why: A ring modulator multiplies two signals, A × B. Where B is 0 the sound is silent, where B is negative it is flipped.
steps.do: Press F2. Hold Ctrl and drag a new cable from OUT of the wavefolder to IN A of the ring modulator. Drag OUT of the ring modulator to IN 1 of the amplifier (it replaces the wavefolder's cable there), and SIN of the LFO to IN B.
steps.after: The notes now pulse in volume: a slow B makes A louder and quieter, a tremolo. The panel says it too: LFO ON B = TREMOLO.

steps.why: What if B is fast enough to hear?
steps.do: Press F1 and turn RATE of the LFO all the way up.
steps.after: The tremolo turned into a clanging, bell-like tone. Multiplying two audible frequencies makes new ones at their sum and difference, which do not fit the note: metal, bells, robot voices. The LFO is now an oscillator: CV and audio are the same voltages, only at different speeds.
steps.try: Turn MIX of the ring modulator: to the left you get A back unchanged, so you can blend in just a bit of the metal.

steps.do: Two ways to make a sound rich: take away from a bright wave, or add to a pure one. Press Next to finish.
